messages.subject: version 0.6-5 of NIMBLE released
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We're pleased to announce that we've released version 0.6-5 of NIMBLE
on CRAN and at R-nimble.org.

Version 0.6-5 is a minor release focused on some bug fixes and CRAN
packaging issues, but there is some new functionality, in particular:

- addition of the functions  c(), seq(), rep(), `:`, diag() for use in
BUGS code;
- addition of two improper distributions (dflat and dhalfflat) as well
as the inverse-Wishart distribution;
- the ability to estimate the asymptotic covariance of the estimates
in NIMBLE's MCEM algorithm;
- the ability to use nimbleLists in any nimbleFunction, newly
including nimbleFunctions without setup code;
- and a variety of bug fixes and better error trapping.

More details on the NIMBLE web page and the NEWS file of the package.

We're also hard at work on a variety of new functionality, including
automatic differentiation, use of optim() within the NIMBLE DSL,
allowing for stochastic indexing (e.g., for mixture models), and
conditional auto-regressive (CAR) models, so the next few releases
should have exciting new capabilities.

- Chris Paciorek for the NIMBLE Development Team

messages.subject: Effective sample size calculation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

just a quick question about how you calculate the effective sample size in the particle filter. Doucet & Johansen* write:

"As we have already mentioned, resampling has the effect of removing particles with low weights and multiplying particles with high weights. However, this is at the cost of immediately introducing some additional variance. If particles have unnormalised weights with a small variance then the resampling step might be unnecessary. Consequently, in practice, it is more sensible to resample only when the variance of the unnor- malised weights is superior to a pre-specified threshold. This is often assessed by looking at the variability of the weights using the so-called Effective Sample Size (ESS) criterion [30, pp. 35-36], which is given (at time n) by..."

This means they use the unnormalised weights to compute the effective sample size = 1/sum(weights^2)

In your algorithm, you compute

    normWts <- exp(wts)/sum(exp(wts))
    ess <<- 1/sum(normWts^2)

which makes sense to me, but now I'm confused. Did I misunderstand the Doucet paper?

cheers,
Andrew

* Doucet, A., & Johansen, A. M. (2009). A tutorial on particle filtering and smoothing: Fifteen years later. Handbook of Nonlinear Filtering.

messages.subject: Re: Effective sample size calculation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

Thanks for the question!  The sentence in Doucet and Johansen that reads "... it is more sensible to resample only when the variance of the unnormalised weights is superior to a pre-specified threshold." does make it seem as though the unnormalised weights should be used in the calculation of the ESS.  However, note that in their paper, I believe that the unnormalised weights are denoted by a lowercase "w", while the normalised weights are denoted by an uppercase "W", and thus it is the normalised weights that are used in their ESS formula.  I think the reasoning behind this is that the variance of the normalised weights is proportional to the variance of the unnormalised weights, and thus the formula they've written could be re-written in terms of the unnormalized weights.  The paper :

A. Kong, J. S. Liu, and W. H. Wong. Sequential imputations and Bayesian missing data problems. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 89(425):278–288, 1994.

defines this estimate of the ESS (specifically in equations 14 and 15) and gives more justification for why ess <<- 1/sum(normWts^2) works and how it relates to the variance of the unnormalised weights.

Nick

messages.subject: eigenvectors in a BUGS function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to write a function for use in BUGS code that internally calculates and uses the first eigenvector of a matrix and returns a scalar.

My impression is that this is not possible because BUGS functions must not have setup code but the dollar sign of eigen(M)$vectors requires setup code.

I've attached a short toy example.

Is there a hack that can overcome this apparent incompatibility?

thanks
David

messages.subject: Re: eigenvectors in a BUGS function
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

In addition to Fritz's comment above, as of NIMBLE v0.6-5, the following model should compile and run:

BUGScode <- nimbleCode ({
    for (ii in 1:D)
        for (jj in 1:D)
            M[ii,jj] ~ dnorm(mean=(ii==jj), sd=sig)
    sumEV <- sum(eigen(M[1:D, 1:D])$vectors[1:D,1])
})

This would save you the trouble of having to use an additional helper function to calculate the sum of the first eigenvector.

Nick
